summary: Turns the search page into a client component. It reads q from the URL, fetches matching products and lists them under a heading that shows the query.

findings.title: Reflected XSS through the search query heading
findings.problem: The heading injects the raw q URL parameter as HTML through dangerouslySetInnerHTML. No code escapes or sanitizes the query first.
findings.consequence: An attacker can send a victim a link whose q value carries script. That script then runs in the victim's session on this origin.
findings.fix: Render the query as a normal text child so React escapes it.

findings.title: Effect without dependencies refetches on every render
findings.problem: The effect has no dependency array, so it runs after every render. Each response calls setResults with a new array, which renders again and starts another fetch.
findings.consequence: The page sends search requests to the catalog API in an endless loop. This loads the backend and drains the user's network and battery.
findings.fix: Give the effect a dependency array containing query.

findings.title: Hooks called after a conditional early return
findings.problem: SearchPage returns early when q is empty, before it calls useState and useEffect. So the number of hooks the component calls changes between renders.
findings.consequence: If the user navigates on the client from no query to a query, React throws because the hook count changed. The search page then crashes.
findings.fix: Call useState and useEffect before the early return. Inside the effect, skip the fetch when query is empty.

findings.title: Search failure leaves an unhandled rejection
findings.problem: searchProducts throws when the response is not ok. The effect chains only then on the promise and never handles the rejection.
findings.consequence: A failed search produces an unhandled rejection. The user sees an empty list with no error message.
findings.fix: Add a catch handler that records the error in state and shows it to the user.

findings.title: List items rendered without a key
findings.problem: The results map renders each li without a key prop. Product has a stable id field that the code could use as the key.
findings.consequence: React logs a missing key warning in development. React also cannot match list items efficiently when the results change.
findings.fix: Set the key of each li to product.id.

findings.title: New search page behaviour has no test
findings.problem: SearchPage now fetches products and renders them from the q parameter. No test file in the change covers this new behaviour.
findings.consequence: Regressions like the fetch loop or the hook order crash can reach users unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add a component test for an empty query, results rendering and a failed search.
